From: Olivia Grant <olivia@bluewaterlabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — SLA carveout request

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're close to an internal buy decision but legal/procurement pushed back on one item: for our private VPC deployment we need clarity in the SLA that latency attributable to customer-controlled network appliances (firewalls, WAF, and egress NAT gateways in our colo) is explicitly excluded from Redwood's P99 latency SLO.

They also asked for an operational runbook hook: in the event Bluewater detects an elevated tail latency incident, we need an agreed evidence collection process and a contact roster for a telemetry handback so we can complete our incident RCA.

Can you share a proposed carveout paragraph and a short runbook excerpt we can include in the contract? Procurement would like something they can attach immediately to the PO.

Appreciate it — Olivia
Olivia Grant
VP Product Operations | Bluewater Labs

Thank you — this is a reasonable ask. I'm attaching a short carveout draft and a clipped runbook extract for your legal team to review. Quick notes up front:

I'll loop in our support and legal leads to make sure the wording is operationally actionable. If procurement wants to move fast I can send a DocuSign-ready appendix once we align on the exact language.

Marissa,
Quick note on telemetry: from our private control plane we can reliably provide:
- Per-request ingress/egress timestamps and request IDs for any call routed through our runtime (we redact PII).
- Token-level latency histograms (p50/p90/p95/p99) by model + route for the requested 72-hour window.
- KV cache hit/miss counts and approximate cache residency time.
- Uploadable logs (syslog snippets) and an image of the deployed model variant and quantization profile.

What we need from Bluewater:
- Packet captures around the same time window (pcap) or flow logs that show internal firewall processing times, and the source NAT timestamps if applicable.
- A short description of any maintenance/ACL rules or WAF rules recently changed.

I recommend we add an objective evidence checklist to the appendix: required customer artifacts + Redwood artifacts. That will avoid back-and-forth when latency is contested. Happy to draft the checklist.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment — SLA carveout request

Marissa / Dylan —
I've put together a short legal paragraph and an operational appendix. Key points:
- Proposed carveout language limits Redwood's latency SLOs to delays \"caused by Redwood-managed runtime and networking\" and excludes delays \"resulting from customer-managed appliances, third-party transit providers, or misconfigurations on the customer's side.\"
- We preserve a 5-business-day joint evidence collection period before any credit is applied; if either party requests an extension for technical reasons, that must be mutually agreed in writing.
- We add an objective artifacts checklist (pcap, flow logs, timestamp mapping table) and a single Slack/phone contact roster for the investigation.

I'll attach the exact wording to the appendix. If legal at Bluewater asks for tighter language on "third-party transit providers" we can enumerate examples, but I'd prefer to keep the initial appendix operationally focused rather than exhaustive.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
